newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt markets end steady after mixed jobs data.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt markets end steady after mixed jobs data.

* NZ debt finishes flat after mixed bag of statistics
* Bank bills ignore currency volatility, remain bid
* Focus expected to turn to U.S. data on Friday
New Zealand debt markets ended steady on Tuesday after a mixed bag of jobs data from Statistics New Zealand.

The December quarter Household Labour Force Survey showed negative employment growth of 0.5 percent in the quarter. Economists forecasts had ranged from a flat figure to 0.6 percent quarterly growth, with an average pick of 0.325 percent.
Equally unexpectedly, unemployment also fell. At 5.9 percent, its lowest level in more than eight years, it compared to 6.3 percent in the September quarter and economists' forecasts of 6.42 percent.

"The market initially bought it on the employment number, and then it came back. On the whole, we've actually closed unchanged," one dealer, adding that volumes had dropped away as the market digested the data.
"The upshot of it was it was almost a neutral number for the market, really. That's how it has been priced."

The 90-day bank bills ended on Monday's close of 7.40 percent. The March futures contract was steady at 92.69 on good volume of 2,666 contracts, and dealers said it continued to be bound in the 92.60-74 range seen over the last couple of weeks.

They said the short end had held in remarkably well given the steep fall of the currency's Trade-Weighted Index in the morning to 67.81 from 68.16 at Monday's close. By Tuesday's close it had bounced back up to 68.25.

"That was very surprising...We came in and the TWI had traded off about 40 points, and the short end was about two points weaker. The market still obviously has a very bid tone, and people are happy to hold long positions even given currency weakness," one dealer said.
With markets shut on Thursday for the Waitangi Day holiday, attention is expected to wander offshore for the remainder of the week.
